senses.gloss: Legal protection that keeps someone from being prosecuted or punished.
examples: The witness testified only after prosecutors granted him *immunity*.
The driver claimed diplomatic *immunity* and was never charged.
The law gives police officers broad *immunity* from such lawsuits.

senses.gloss: The form of a verb used to give an order or an instruction.
examples: In "Close the door," the verb is an *imperative*.
Recipes are almost always written in the *imperative*.
The teacher showed us how to form *imperatives* in Spanish.

senses.gloss: A tool or utensil used for a particular job.
examples: Keep the writing *implements* in the top drawer.
A whisk is the right *implement* for the job.
The museum displays stone *implements* made thousands of years ago.

senses.gloss: The act of officially putting a tax, rule, or penalty into effect.
examples: The *imposition* of a curfew angered residents.
Farmers fought the *imposition* of the new tariff.
The judge explained the *imposition* of the fine.

senses.gloss: A funny imitation of the way a well-known person talks and acts.
examples: He does a great *impression* of the president.
Her *impression* of our boss had the whole office laughing.
The comedian is famous for his celebrity *impressions*.

senses.gloss: A mark left when something is pressed into a soft surface.
examples: The dentist made an *impression* of my teeth.
You could see the *impression* of a boot in the mud.
The seal left a clear *impression* in the wax.

senses.gloss: The act of putting someone or something into a group, a list, or a total.
examples: The *inclusion* of her name on the guest list surprised everyone.
Several senators objected to the *inclusion* of the tax break in the bill.
His *inclusion* on the roster was never in doubt.

senses.gloss: The ability to support yourself and make your own decisions without help from others.
examples: After the stroke, he fought to keep his *independence*.
A used car gave her a new sense of *independence*.
The program helps young adults build financial *independence*.

senses.gloss: A sign that something has failed badly and deserves harsh criticism.
examples: The report is a damning *indictment* of the agency's safety record.
Six-hour waits are an *indictment* of the whole system.
Critics called the movie an *indictment* of American greed.

senses.gloss: In mathematics, a statement that one quantity is larger or smaller than another.
examples: He wrote the *inequality* x > 5 on the board.
Solve the *inequality* and graph it on a number line.
The homework was ten *inequalities* to solve.

senses.gloss: The filling of something with air or gas.
examples: The manual lists the correct *inflation* pressure for each tire.
The balloon burst during *inflation*.
Proper *inflation* makes your tires last longer.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that affects how someone behaves or develops.
examples: His older brother was a bad *influence* on him.
She was the biggest *influence* on my writing.
Blues and gospel were early *influences* on the band.

senses.gloss: One of the parts or qualities that make something work or succeed.
examples: Trust is the key *ingredient* in any partnership.
The town has all the *ingredients* of a great weekend trip.
Hard work is only one *ingredient* of success.

senses.gloss: A sudden addition of money into a business, a project, or an economy.
examples: The startup survived on a last-minute *injection* of cash.
The transit system needs a major *injection* of federal money.
Two capital *injections* kept the airline flying.

senses.gloss: A lack of experience of the harder or uglier parts of life.
examples: The photographs capture the *innocence* of childhood.
He lost his *innocence* the summer his father left.
There is a sweet *innocence* about the way she asks questions.

senses.gloss: The state of not being safe or not being guaranteed.
examples: Food *insecurity* affects one in ten households in the county.
Housing *insecurity* has risen sharply since the plant closed.
Job *insecurity* kept them from buying a house.

senses.gloss: A large piece of modern art built for a particular space.
examples: The museum's new *installation* fills the entire lobby.
Her *installation* uses mirrors and recorded voices.
We spent an hour walking through the light *installations*.

senses.gloss: One part of a story, series, or set of movies released over time.
examples: The next *installment* of the series comes out in June.
I read the final *installment* of her column this morning.
Each *installment* ends on a cliffhanger.

senses.gloss: A custom or practice that has been an important part of a society for a long time.
examples: The *institution* of marriage has changed a great deal in fifty years.
Historians trace how the *institution* of slavery shaped the South.
Friday night football is a small-town *institution*.

senses.gloss: Something you do or keep as protection in case things go wrong.
examples: I packed a second flashlight as *insurance*.
He saved the emails as *insurance* in case anyone denied it.
Three months' pay in the bank is cheap *insurance* against a layoff.

senses.gloss: The state of being whole, sound, and undamaged.
examples: Engineers questioned the structural *integrity* of the bridge.
The fire damaged the *integrity* of the roof beams.
Encryption protects the *integrity* of the data.

senses.gloss: The act of stopping or catching something while it is on its way somewhere.
examples: The *interception* of the shipment led to six arrests.
The court set limits on the *interception* of private messages.
Radar made *interception* of the plane possible.

senses.gloss: A feeling of wanting to know about something or take part in it.
examples: She has had an *interest* in birds since she was a child.
His main *interests* are hiking and photography.
The class lost *interest* halfway through the video.

senses.gloss: A legal share in a business or a piece of property.
examples: He sold his *interest* in the restaurant last spring.
The family holds a controlling *interest* in the newspaper.
The judge disclosed a financial *interest* in the company.

senses.gloss: The point or area where two things meet and affect each other.
examples: Her research sits at the *interface* of medicine and law.
Scientists study the *interface* between the ice and the ocean.
The clinic works at the *interface* of housing and health care.

senses.gloss: Unwanted involvement in someone else's affairs or in a process.
examples: The report found no evidence of foreign *interference* in the election.
She resented her mother-in-law's constant *interference*.
The judge warned him against *interference* with the investigation.

senses.gloss: The inland part of a country or region, away from the coast.
examples: Most of the state's wheat is grown in the *interior*.
Small planes fly supplies into the *interior*.
Roads in the *interior* are mostly gravel.

senses.gloss: A short period of time between two longer or busier ones.
examples: The rain gave us a quiet *interlude* before the crowds arrived.
After a brief *interlude* in Texas, the family moved back east.
Those two years were a happy *interlude* in a hard decade.

senses.gloss: A planned meeting in which family and friends confront someone about a drinking or drug problem.
examples: His sisters staged an *intervention* over Thanksgiving.
A counselor walked the family through how an *intervention* works.
After the *intervention* he agreed to go to rehab.

senses.gloss: A conversation in which a reporter asks someone questions to be printed or broadcast.
examples: The mayor gave an *interview* to the local paper.
In a rare television *interview*, she talked about her illness.
He turned down all *interviews* after the trial.

senses.gloss: The act of telling two people each other's names so that they can meet.
examples: Let me make the *introductions*.
We met through a mutual friend's *introduction*.
She was too shy to wait for an *introduction*.

senses.gloss: The bringing of something new into use or into a place.
examples: The *introduction* of the smartphone changed everything.
The *introduction* of rabbits to Australia was a disaster.
Sales fell right after the *introduction* of the new fee.
